search_bias: evaluation/verifiers; measurement-validity/benchmark-design; finite-horizon power and resolution of exact paired sequential e-processes

sources_checked_or_revisited.title: Estimating means of bounded random variables by betting
sources_checked_or_revisited.relevance: Confirms predictable betting strategies must use only past information, mixture and predictable plug-in constructions are valid sequential approaches, and Ville-style thresholding gives arbitrary-stopping validity.

sources_checked_or_revisited.title: Game-Theoretic Statistics and Safe Anytime-Valid Inference
sources_checked_or_revisited.authors: Aaditya Ramdas, Peter Grünwald, Vladimir Vovk, Glenn Shafer
sources_checked_or_revisited.relevance: Reconfirms that e-process/test-martingale wealth may be monitored continuously and that power depends on the betting strategy even when validity does not.

simulation.purpose: Resolve the prior frontier: compare fixed, predictable plug-in and mixture sequential McNemar-style e-processes at only 10-50 completed task pairs under varying discordance rates.

design.task_model: Each task is concordant with probability 1-r and contributes factor 1. If discordant, candidate wins with probability p and loses with probability 1-p. Tasks are independent outer units in this simulation.

methods.mix: equal-weight mixture of fixed-q e-processes q in {0.55,0.60,...,0.95}

design.note: Monte Carlo verifies behavior/power only; exact Type-I validity comes from the e-process construction, not from the simulation.

aggressive_fixed_bet_tail_example.interpretation: A very aggressive fixed bet can increase probability of a lucky threshold crossing by a short horizon while making typical evidence much worse. Finite-horizon rejection probability and expected/typical log-wealth are different optimization objectives.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Select the betting strategy against the operational evaluation objective, not a generic notion of power. Expected log-growth for a fixed alternative is maximized near q=p, but finite-horizon probability of ever crossing a rejection threshold can favor substantially more aggressive q because it rewards lucky paths and ignores wealth collapse on unresolved paths.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: In r=0.2,p=0.7,N=50 simulations, q=0.95 crossed by N about 20.1% versus q=0.70 about 5.2%, yet q=0.95 had median final e=0.130 and mean log e=-2.427 versus q=0.70 median e=2.277 and mean log e=0.819. Both remain valid e-process bets under the conditional null; the difference is utility/risk profile, not Type-I validity.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: Simulation assumes independent completed task pairs and a stable discordance rate/sign probability. This is a design diagnostic, not a claim that q=0.95 is generally preferable.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.implication: Report unresolved fraction and final evidence distribution, not only 'detected by deadline'. A benchmark optimizer that chooses the betting rule solely for deadline-crossing probability can create a high-variance evaluation gate.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: At only 10-50 task pairs, a predictable plug-in initialized at q=0.5 can spend too much of the scarce evidence budget learning the alternative. A prior-hedged plug-in or a predeclared mixture buys earlier sensitivity without invalidating optional stopping; fixed-q can dominate later when its target is well matched.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: At r=0.4,p=0.8, stop probability at N=10/20/30/50 was fixed 0.0022/0.1239/0.3702/0.7251, hedged 0.0442/0.2470/0.3942/0.6396, naive Jeffreys 0.0119/0.1666/0.2984/0.5433, and mixture 0.0119/0.2042/0.4000/0.6602. Ranking changes with horizon. At sparse r=0.2,p=0.9,N=50, hedged 0.608 and mixture 0.593 exceeded fixed 0.497 and naive plug-in 0.504.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: The hedged prior q0=0.75,strength=4 and the discrete mixture grid were chosen for this experiment; different priors/grids can change rankings. The result supports horizon-aware calibration experiments, not one universal bettor.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.implication: When independent task count is only 10-50, pre-register or calibrate a small bettor family against realistic effect/discordance regimes, then preserve validity by keeping all adaptation predictable or by mixing valid e-processes.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: For paired sequential evaluation, report at least: total tasks, discordant tasks/rate, probability/fraction resolved by each planned decision horizon, unresolved fraction, and a distributional summary of final e-value/log-wealth on unresolved paths. Conditional median stopping time alone is selection-biased toward paths that happened to cross.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: The same simulation exhibits strategy crossovers by horizon and aggressive-bet cases where crossing probability improves while median/mean log evidence deteriorates. Thus a single 'median stopping time among stopped runs' can rank methods misleadingly.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: This is a reporting/measurement-validity recommendation for sequential benchmark experiments; exact fields can be adapted for nonbinary rewards.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.implication: Evaluation papers should separate validity, deadline-resolution probability, evidence stability, and information availability instead of compressing them into one speed number.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: The fixed bet q matching the true alternative p must maximize finite-horizon stopping probability.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. It maximizes expected log growth per discordance under the simple stationary alternative, but a high-variance aggressive bet can have greater probability of an early lucky threshold crossing while producing much worse typical wealth.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: A predictable plug-in is automatically the best default when the alternative effect is unknown.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. Predictability establishes validity, not finite-budget efficiency. The naive Jeffreys-style plug-in was materially underpowered in several 10-50-task scenarios because it begins at q=0.5; prior hedging or mixtures can improve short-horizon resolution.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: The bettor with the smallest conditional median stopping time is the best sequential evaluator.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. Conditional stopping-time summaries omit unresolved paths and can reward high-variance strategies. Resolution probability and unresolved evidence distribution must be reported jointly.

design_implications.validity_vs_utility: Keep the exact e-process validity proof separate from bettor selection. Choose bettor using predeclared utility criteria and realistic task/discordance regimes.
design_implications.small_budget_default: For 10-50 independent task pairs and unknown effect size, compare a conservative fixed bet, a prior-hedged predictable plug-in, and a small discrete mixture before deployment; do not assume naive plug-in dominance.
design_implications.reporting: Always report unresolved fraction and discordance information alongside stopping-time summaries.
design_implications.anti_pseudoreplication: Internal correlated rollouts remain one outer task unit unless stronger justified structure exists.

frontier_queue.action: Optimize prior strength/center and mixture grid under explicit minimax or Bayes utility over plausible discordance/effect/horizon distributions, while constraining downside evidence instability; compare against fixed q and oracle expected-log-growth q.

Derive a computationally explicit backward recursion for the induced anytime-valid exact McNemar terminal test at fixed N and compare its early stopping boundary/power with forward betting strategies.
Construct symmetric within-task adaptive rollout finalization policies and counterexamples where equal single-rollout marginals fail to imply symmetric finalized task outcomes.
Extend bettor-utility analysis to bounded paired reward differences and weak average nulls, including heterogeneous task strata and realistic benchmark sampling.

early_termination_avoidance: The prior exact sequential paired-binary construction now has finite-budget power diagnostics, but bettor selection exhibits strong horizon/objective dependence and the induced exact terminal-McNemar route remains unresolved. Continue rather than treating this simulation as completion.
exact_next_action: Derive the finite-horizon backward recursion for terminal exact McNemar and, in parallel, formulate an explicit minimax/Bayes objective for choosing a prior-hedged or mixture bettor when only 10-50 independent task pairs are available.
